source: WHO-TM2 / Natural Medicines Database / Stockley's Herbal Medicines Interactions (representative subset)

interactions.clinical_effect: Significantly reduces plasma levels of affected drugs, leading to therapeutic failure (e.g. INR drop, transplant rejection, HIV virologic failure, contraceptive failure, serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs).
interactions.management: Avoid concurrent use. If unavoidable, increase monitoring (INR, drug levels). Counsel patient on contraceptive failure risk.

interactions.clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk with anticoagulants/antiplatelets. High-dose garlic may reduce saquinavir levels via CYP3A4.
interactions.management: Monitor INR closely. Advise patients to disclose garlic supplement use before surgery.

interactions.clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk. Case reports of seizures with valproate. Possible serotonin syndrome with SSRIs.
interactions.management: Monitor coagulation. Avoid in patients on antiepileptics with narrow therapeutic window.

interactions.clinical_effect: Dangerous additive sedation, respiratory depression. Hepatotoxicity risk (direct + additive with hepatotoxic drugs).
interactions.management: Contraindicated with CNS depressants. Stop at least 24 h before anaesthesia. Liver function monitoring.
Taper valerian before elective surgery. Inform anaesthetist.

interactions.clinical_effect: May antagonise immunosuppression. Possible additive hepatotoxicity with methotrexate.
interactions.management: Avoid in transplant patients or anyone on immunosuppression.

interactions.clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk. Additive hypoglycaemic effect with antidiabetics. Worsens INR variability.
interactions.management: Monitor blood glucose and INR closely. Advise diabetic patients to report hypoglycaemic episodes.

interactions.clinical_effect: Sodium retention, hypokalaemia, oedema — antagonises antihypertensives. Potassium depletion potentiates digoxin toxicity.
interactions.management: Avoid in hypertensive patients. Monitor electrolytes and digoxin levels.

interactions.clinical_effect: Mild increased bleeding risk at high supplemental doses. May slightly potentiate antidiabetics.
interactions.management: Informational alert at culinary doses. Monitor INR with supplemental doses (>1 g/day curcumin).

interactions.clinical_effect: Additive hypoglycaemia. Laxative effect depletes potassium → digoxin toxicity risk.
interactions.management: Avoid prolonged oral use with antidiabetics/digoxin. Monitor electrolytes.

interactions.clinical_effect: May reduce plasma ARV levels → HIV virologic failure. Commonly used in Southern Africa alongside ART.
interactions.management: Strongly advise against concurrent use. Document and escalate to HIV clinician.
